\[
g_C = \frac{Y_n}{n_C},
\quad
Y_n = 0.2126\, n_R + 0.7152\, n_G + 0.0722\, n_B,
\quad
C' = \begin{cases} \operatorname{srgb}\left(g_C \operatorname{lin}(C)\right) & \text{linear light} \\ g_C\, C & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(n_C\): Channel C of the neutral color
- \(Y_n\): The luminance of the neutral color
- \(g_C\): The gain of channel C

n is the picked neutral color and Y_n its luminance, with the BT.709 weights. The gain of each channel turns the neutral into the gray (Y_n, Y_n, Y_n), so it keeps its brightness and loses its color. All other colors get the same gains, which is the von Kries idea of scaling each channel on its own. With Linear light on, the default, the gains act on linear light values: decoded from sRGB, scaled, and encoded again. A change in the color of the light scales linear values, so this is the physical model. With it off, the gains scale the encoded values. A channel of the neutral at 0 gets gain 1.
